claims.text: Adding a small fraction of Yttrium to a Zr–Cu–Ni–Al metallic-glass alloy enhances its glass-forming ability.
Yttrium addition increases atomic-size mismatch in the Zr–Cu–Ni–Al alloy.
Yttrium addition makes the relevant heats of mixing more negative in the Zr–Cu–Ni–Al alloy.
Atomic-size difference and mixing enthalpy are thermophysical parameters that affect phase formation.
Increased atomic-size mismatch and negative heats of mixing suppress crystallization during rapid solidification.
The initial Zr–Cu–Ni–Al alloy tends to crystallize or forms only a marginally stable amorphous structure under standard processing conditions.
Approximately 3 at% Yttrium is an effective modification level for the base alloy.
High cooling rates permit the Yttrium additive to affect crystal nucleation and growth.
Yttrium modifies local chemical interactions and disrupts the long-range atomic order required for crystallization.
The size difference and mixing enthalpy of Yttrium with the base elements make Yttrium atoms obstacles to crystal nucleation and growth.
The proposed disruption of nucleation and growth increases the supercooled-liquid region.
Increasing the supercooled-liquid region stabilizes the amorphous state.
The Yttrium-modified alloy will have a wider supercooled-liquid region than the Yttrium-free base alloy under equivalent rapid-solidification conditions.
The Yttrium-modified alloy will resist crystallization more strongly than the Yttrium-free base alloy under equivalent rapid-solidification conditions.
The beneficial effect of Yttrium is anticipated specifically under rapid-cooling conditions.
